name: create_or_update_routine
description:
Author or edit a routine's if/then/else automation logic, as a small restricted Python-like snippet (not executed -- deterministically compiled into NuCore's routine schema). Use routine_status_op instead to change a routine's enabled/running state without changing its logic. Use variable_op to create/update/delete a NuCore variable itself (not its role inside routine logic). If the hub rejects a save (compile succeeds but create/update fails), the returned error includes the hub's own errorCode/errorMessage (e.g. `BadRequestError: Invalid program`) -- read it, fix the specific problem it names, and retry once with corrected `code` rather than giving up or repeating the same call unchanged. UPDATING AN EXISTING ROUTINE (id given): `code` REPLACES the routine's entire if/then/else content -- there is no partial-patch mode. Before writing an update, call get_routine_detail(id) first and base your new `code` on its actual current logic, preserving whatever the customer didn't ask to change. Never write update code from memory of an earlier turn or from what ROUTINES DATABASE's summary implies -- both can be stale or incomplete, and writing code without checking current content risks silently deleting conditions/actions the customer wanted kept. NOTE: unlike this system's other tools, this DSL needs real property/parameter/routine/variable ids and uom/precision values (not display names) -- fidelity the compact DEVICE DATABASE deliberately does not carry -- with ONE exception: a property or command itself is referenced by its exact display NAME (never its id) in status()/was_controlled()/command()/adjust_scene(command=...) -- the backend resolves the real id server-side, so there's no id to look up or get wrong for those. A command's PARAMETER id (inside params=[param(id=..., ...)]) is still a real id, not a name. Before writing any status()/was_controlled()/command()/param() call for a device, call get_device_detail(device_id) for that device first and use the exact property/command names and parameter ids/uom/precision it returns -- never guess them, and never reuse values from an earlier turn's routine (call it fresh for this device, this turn, even if you've referenced the same device before). Routine ids (for schedule's lastruntime=, routine_is_true/routine_is_false, run_if/run_then/run_else/enable_routine/disable_routine/stop_routine/enable_run_at_startup/disable_run_at_startup) come from ROUTINES DATABASE. Variable ids/types/precisions come from list_variables -- never invented, never asked of the customer if the variable is already known. X10 house/unit/command codes and notification recipient ids still have no lookup source in this system -- only use them if the customer states the exact id/code themselves; otherwise ask. A routine has exactly ONE comment: the `comment` input field on this tool, never anything written inline in `code`. Do not write bare strings as conditions or actions to leave yourself notes -- they are not a supported construct there (the compiler silently drops any it finds); put explanatory text in `comment` instead. GRAMMAR: `code` is either (1) exactly one top-level `if : else: ` (the `else:` is optional -- omit it entirely rather than writing `else: pass`), or (2) a condition-less sequence of only action statements (no `if` at all) when the user wants a routine/macro with no trigger. No other top-level statements are allowed: no imports, assignments, elif, real while/for loops, or function/class definitions. CONDITIONS (the `if` line) -- combine with plain Python `and`/`or`/parentheses only: - Property comparison: `device("").status("", uom=, precision=) ` where `` is `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==`, or `!=`. `` is the exact display name from get_device_detail's 'properties' list (not an id). - Physical control event: `device("").was_controlled(command="", eq="is")` or `eq="isnot"` (defaults to "is"). `` is the exact display name from get_device_detail's 'sends' list (not an id) -- this checks what the device itself sent. No params= -- this schema can only check whether the command was sent, not a parameter value. - Schedule (pick exactly one time reference per call -- never combine time=/sunrise=/sunset=/lastruntime=): `at(time="HH:MM:SS")`, `at(sunrise=duration(minute=-10))`, `at(sunset=duration(minute=10), date="YYYY/MM/DD")`, `at(lastruntime=, offset=duration(minute=5), daily=True)` (relative to when that OTHER routine last ran), `weekly_at(days="mon,wed", time="HH:MM:SS")`, `weekly_between(days="tue", from_sunset=duration(minute=-10), to_time="01:00:00", to_day=1)`, `weekly_for(days="mon,wed,fri", from_sunrise=duration(minute=30), duration=duration(hour=2))`, `between(from_time="08:00:00", from_date="YYYY/MM/DD", to_time="17:00:00", to_date="YYYY/MM/DD")`. `days=` is a comma-separated subset of sun,mon,tue,wed,thu,fri,sat, lowercase. `to_day=` is an integer day offset (0=same day), only valid on the "to" side. Use weekly_between/weekly_for/between (not two at/weekly_at joined by and) for any duration/window; use at/weekly_at only for a single point in time. A customer request for N known future one-off dates (e.g. a list of specific calendar dates you already computed, such as from a Hebrew-calendar plugin) is ONE routine with N `at(date=...)` conditions joined by `or` -- see the third EXAMPLE below -- never N separate routines; the `or` combinator applies to schedule conditions exactly like any other condition. - Another routine's current state: `routine_is_true()` / `routine_is_false()`. - NuCore variable comparison (real id/type/precision from list_variables): `var_ref(id=, type=1, precision=

) ` (type: 1=integer variable, 2=state variable) -- `` is a plain number, scaled by precision= exactly like a device param's value= is scaled by its precision=, or another `var_ref(id=.., type=.., precision=..)`. - Legacy X10 event (only if the customer states the real codes -- no lookup tool exists for these): `x10_event(house="B", command=2)` or with `unit=3`, `eq="is"`/`"isnot"`. `house` is a single letter A-P, `command` is 0-15, `unit` is 1-16. - Utility demand-response signal: `utility_price(op=">", value=0.25)` (op is >,>=,<,<=,==,!=), `utility_status(op="is", value="active")` (value: inactive/active/pendingVeryNear/pendingNear/pendingFar/pendingVeryFar), `utility_mode(op="is", value="normal")` (value: none/normal/moderate/high/special). - All durations (wait, repeat interval, sunrise/sunset/lastruntime offset) use `duration(hour=, minute=, second=)`, every argument optional and defaulting to 0 -- write the numbers exactly as stated (`duration(minute=90)` is fine), never do the unit math yourself. Negative means before an event, positive means after. ACTIONS (the `then:`/`else:` body, executed top-to-bottom as a flat sequence -- NOT Python control flow): - `device("").command("")` or with `params=[param(id="", value=, uom=, precision=), ...]` -- always a list, even for one parameter; omit `params=` entirely for a parameterless command; `"n/a"` is a valid `id` for an anonymous parameter. `` is the exact display name from get_device_detail's 'accepts' list (not an id) -- e.g. `.command("On")`, never `.command("DON")`. The parameter's own `id=` (inside `param(...)`) IS still a real id from that same 'accepts' entry. - `wait(duration(minute=))`, optionally `random=True` for a random duration between 0 and that value. Only include a wait when the customer explicitly asked for a delay, or the action is a deliberate flash/pulse (on then immediately off) -- never as a generic pause between adjacent commands. - Repeat: `repeat(count=)` or `repeat(count=, random=True)`, or `every(duration(hour=2))`, or `while_repeat(id=, type=1, op=">", value=0, precision=

)` (repeats while that variable comparison holds; precision= required, same scaling rule as var_ref/set_var). **CRITICAL: these are markers, not loops with a body** -- every action written AFTER a repeat()/every()/while_repeat() call, for the rest of the SAME then/else list, is what gets repeated. Never write Python `for`/`while` syntax here. - NuCore variable assignment (real id/type/precision from list_variables): `set_var(id=, type=1, op="=", value=, precision=

)` -- `op` is one of `=`,`+=`,`-=`,`*=`,`/=`,`%=`,`&=`,`|=`,`^=`,`"random"`,`"init"`. `op="init"` restores the variable from its stored init value and takes NO source at all -- omit value=/var=/device=/sysval=/precision= entirely for it. For every other op, exactly one source: `value=` with required precision=

(a literal, scaled by that precision, same as a device param's value=), `var=var_ref(id=.., type=.., precision=..)` (another variable -- its own value is used as-is, no separate precision= on set_var itself), `device="", property="", uom=` (a live device-property snapshot -- `` is the exact display name from that device's get_device_detail 'properties' list, not an id), or `sysval=""` (one of SecondsSinceStartOfDay, MinutesSinceStartOfDay, CurrentDayOfYear, CurrentDayOfMonth, CurrentDayOfWeek, CurrentYear, CurrentMonth, CurrentHour, CurrentMinute, CurrentSecond, SunriseToday, SunsetToday, SunriseTomorrow, SunsetTomorrow, UnixDateTime). - Notification (only if the customer states the real recipient id): `notify(recipient=)`, optionally `content=`. - Control another routine: `run_if()`, `run_then()`, `run_else()`, `enable_routine()`, `disable_routine()`, `stop_routine()`, `enable_run_at_startup()`, `disable_run_at_startup()`. - Adjust a group/scene member's link behavior: `adjust_scene(group="", controller="", node="", type="cmd"|"default"|"ignore")`, optionally with `command=""` and `params=[param(...)]` when `type="cmd"` (params= requires command= too). `` is the exact display name from the RESPONDER (`node=`) device's get_device_detail 'accepts' list, not an id. `controller` can be a device id or the scene's own id. - Legacy X10 command (only if the customer states the real codes): `x10_send(house="B", command=2)`, optionally `unit=3`. - System command: `restart_hub()` or `demand_price_alert()` -- no arguments. - Query all properties for a group: `query_all(group="")` (defaults property to "ST") or `query_all(group="", property="")`. EXAMPLE: ```python if device("ZY004_1").status("Status", uom=17, precision=0) > 75 and weekly_at(days="mon,wed,fri", time="18:00:00"): device("25 80 3C 1").command("On", params=[param(id="n/a", value=100, uom=51, precision=0)]) wait(duration(minute=10)) device("25 80 3C 1").command("Off") else: device("25 80 3C 1").command("Off") ``` EXAMPLE (repeat -- note the marker comes FIRST, immediately before the actions it repeats; a customer narrating "turn on, wait, turn off, repeat 5 times" describes the repeat LAST, but the DSL requires it FIRST -- putting it last, after the actions, is the single most common mistake with this construct and compiles to a repeat of nothing): ```python if weekly_at(days="mon,tue", time="05:00:00"): repeat(count=5) device("17 F8 44 1").command("On") wait(duration(minute=1)) device("17 F8 44 1").command("Off") ``` EXAMPLE (N known future one-off dates in ONE routine -- e.g. 10 years of a computed holiday date -- never create N separate routines for this, join the `at(date=...)` conditions with `or` in a single routine instead): ```python if at(date="2026/09/20", time="07:00:00") or at(date="2027/10/10", time="07:00:00") or at(date="2028/09/29", time="07:00:00"): notify(recipient=) ``` INVALID: anything beyond a single top-level if/else or condition-less action sequence; an undocumented function or unknown device/property/command/routine/variable id; `value=`/`uom=`/`precision=` passed directly to `.command(...)`/`.was_controlled(...)` instead of through `params=[param(...)]`; `params=` on `was_controlled(...)`; Python `for`/`while` loop syntax anywhere (use repeat()/every()/while_repeat() as flat markers instead); splitting one continuous schedule window into two calls joined by and/or; more than one of time=/sunrise=/sunset=/lastruntime= in one schedule reference; a raw number instead of `duration(...)` anywhere a duration is expected; more than one source (value=/var=/device=/sysval=) on set_var(...). On any of these, or if a needed device/routine/variable id or value is unclear, ask for clarification instead of guessing.

id.description: Real routine id to edit, exactly as shown in ROUTINES DATABASE, or omit/null when creating a new routine.

comment.description: A short description of what this routine does.

code.description: The routine logic, following the grammar described above.
